knowledge_gaps: Causal prefix scoring does not remove the target transition from the graph built from all training histories. This is permitted training data, but self-contribution can create a memorization shortcut for rare edges. Compare ordinary counts with leave-one-user-out counts or cross-fitted graph features.

The scoring specification lacks concrete values or search ranges for smoothing alpha, popularity floor, clipping threshold, history length, decay and residual weight. Unseen sources, zero-count destinations and repeated history items also need explicit handling.

For a missing edge, log-lift equals log(alpha/(source_count+alpha)), independent of the candidate. This term cancels in ranking; the residual effectively supplies bonuses for observed edges. Rare observed transitions can receive large bonuses, requiring support-sensitive controls.

Decay applies only to the added graph branch. It does not directly reduce older or incidental interactions within SASRec, so claims about correcting historical influence need narrower wording or a separate recency ablation.

Uniform negatives conditioned on excluding each user's training positives are not an unrestricted uniform catalog sample. Specify replacement, duplicate handling, temperature and whether the objective is candidate-set cross-entropy or an importance-corrected sampled-softmax estimator.

Difficulty 4/10 may understate sparse graph lookup across every training position and full-catalog simulator inference. Tensor shapes, efficient lookup, serialization and the history-carrying diagnostic interface remain unspecified.

The experiment plan lacks runtime allocations, validation frequency and a bounded hyperparameter search. Repeated selection on 200 users per category risks validation overfitting; small HR@10 differences require paired uncertainty estimates. The originality rating is reasonable, while potential 8/10 remains speculative.

follow_up_queries.reason: Determine how to prevent target self-contribution and rare-edge memorization while preserving training-only data use; identify stronger simple baselines.
follow_up_queries.query: In sequential recommendation, how do training-derived item-transition graphs handle a training example's own target edge? Find leave-one-user-out or cross-fitted graph-feature methods, confidence shrinkage for sparse transition lift, and comparisons with first-order Markov, FPMC and item-kNN residual baselines.

follow_up_queries.reason: Resolve objective ambiguity and assess whether the proposed implementation fits the compute budget.
follow_up_queries.query: For SASRec with 32–64 negatives per sequence position, what distinguishes candidate-set cross-entropy from importance-corrected sampled softmax when negatives exclude user training positives? Find reproducible sampling, duplicate masking and temperature specifications, plus efficient sparse transition-score lookup for batched training and full-catalog inference.

follow_up_queries.reason: Make model selection reproducible and limit overfitting to the small pinned validation sample.
follow_up_queries.query: For sequential recommendation evaluated by macro HR@10 across four datasets with 200 validation users each and fixed 99-negative candidate sets, how should paired bootstrap uncertainty and repeated hyperparameter-selection bias be assessed? Find budget-aware protocols for comparing baseline, loss-only, graph-only and combined models without accessing test labels.
